body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Thursday, August 20, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high of 104° and air quality at a moderate 74. Overnight, a train struck a pedestrian in south Bakersfield, and a vehicle-versus-pedestrian collision downtown left a pedestrian down at the scene. We’ll have more on those incidents in just a moment. Today’s top story: COVID infections are rising across the country, but a local ER doctor says there’s no reason for Kern County residents to panic just yet. Let’s get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most significant incident unfolded just before 11:34 p.m., when a train struck a pedestrian near the rail line off Lynwood and Height streets in south Bakersfield. Fire crews from Engines 37, 34, and 33 responded with Battalion 3, working to access the patient on the far side of the train. Meanwhile, downtown, a vehicle-versus-pedestrian collision around 9:22 p.m. left a pedestrian down at the scene near Main Street; officers archived surveillance video as part of their investigation. In other parts of the county, a domestic call on Butterfield Avenue escalated just after 12:39 a.m., when a man struck a woman and attempted to take an infant. A heavy-duty response was requested, with a kitchen knife mentioned on the air. Elsewhere, a burglary at a furniture business on Baker Street had suspects possibly still inside around 9:19 p.m., with a silver Prius spotted in an alleyway nearby. Officers set a perimeter at Baker and Kentucky with a second boundary at Baker and Jackson. Just before midnight, a person in crisis on Di Giorgio Road reportedly made threats against family members and was possibly in possession of a knife, with a child present in the residence. The night also included a disturbance at a Washington Avenue apartment, an automatic fire alarm at a Greenfield preschool on South Union Avenue, flooding inside a home on Pinehurst Drive, a welfare check in the 1200 block of East 18th Street that found a juvenile with visible injuries, a smoking semi checked on Highway 58 near the 223 area, and reports of vehicles racing.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 104° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 75° at Meadows Field (KBFL), with no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is at a moderate 74, and there are no active fires to report in the area.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that COVID infections are growing in all 50 states, but a local ER doctor says there’s no reason to panic.** The CDC’s latest data show COVID infections are trending up across the country, including in California. However, Dr. Willie Franklin, with Adventist Health, says he hasn’t yet seen a large increase in COVID patients in Kern County. He notes that while the CDC classifies the trend as up, COVID is responsible for just 0.3% of emergency department visits nationwide—a level considered very low. Dr. Franklin advises that people who are sick or around vulnerable individuals can take simple steps to limit the spread, such as wearing a mask.

**According to 23ABC, Bakersfield residents are raising privacy concerns over the Flock camera network logging 850K plate reads a month.** The Bakersfield Police Department’s transparency portal shows that Flock cameras capture license plate and vehicle information 24 hours a day, with more than 850,000 plate reads in the last 30 days. While BPD describes the cameras as an investigative tool used to help locate stolen vehicles, missing people, and vehicles connected to crimes, residents and organizers at a recent community meeting questioned who can access the data collected. Ariel Dyer, co-founder of the Anti-Capitalist Computer Club, said the timing of the meeting was intentional, coinciding with the National Week of Action against automated license plate readers.

**KGET 17 tells us that a Bakersfield resident won a $350K slot jackpot at Hard Rock Casino Tejon.** This exciting win highlights a positive moment for a local community member.

## Something good

A Bakersfield resident is celebrating a big win after hitting a $350K slot jackpot at Hard Rock Casino Tejon. It’s always uplifting to hear about a local resident’s good fortune, and we hope this win brings plenty of joy.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, the Planning Commission will meet today, August 20, at 5:30 p.m. Later in the week, the City Council will hold two meetings on August 26—one at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater has a busy schedule: Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, and Grupo Yndio will perform on August 22; a Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026-2027 will be available on August 24; Rodney Carrington takes the stage on August 27; CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE happens on August 28; and both Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will perform on August 29. Be sure to check the Fox Theater’s website for tickets and more information.
